grammarSchedule.why: `already`, `since` and `for` are all A1/A2, so the core is writable from lesson 1; lesson 31 adds `ever`, which the superlative use (`the best film I have ever seen`) and `have you ever...?` both need
`for`, `since`, `to work`, `to wait` and `to study` are all prior-level, so `I have been studying English for three years` is writable immediately
`when`, `already` and every common past participle come from A1/A2; `When I arrived, the film had already started` needs nothing from B1
`tired`, `all night`, `to work` are prior-level; lesson 26 (`mind and body`) and lesson 38 (`weight, health and nerves`) later give the writer better causes to explain
`if` (A2) and `will` (A1) are both prior; `If it rains tomorrow, we will stay home` is writable from the start
`if` (A2) and `would` (A2) are prior; lesson 3 (`making a decision`) and lesson 33 (`plans, dates and deadlines`) supply the imagined situations
needs only `if` plus have/had and a past participle, all prior-level; lesson 13 (`saying sorry and admitting`) makes the regret reading natural
`unless` is a B1 concept and is introduced in lesson 28 (`conditions and exceptions`), together with `even if`, `in case`, `as long as` and `as far as`
the pattern is be + past participle; `to repair`, `to build`, `to finish` and `bridge`/`report` are all prior-level
`must`, `can` and `should` are A1, so `The homework must be finished by Monday` needs no B1 word
`to get` is A1 and `to lose`, `to break`, `to pay` are A2; lesson 70 (`accidents`) and lesson 88 in the final order add sudden events to talk about
`to say`, `to tell` and `that` are A1; the backshift itself is a form change, not vocabulary
`to ask` (A2), `whether` (A2), `if` (A2) and the wh-words are all prior-level
`would` is A2 and `to help`, `to say` are A1; nothing at B1 is needed
`should` is A1; lesson 13 (`saying sorry and admitting`) gives `to apologize` and `to admit` for the regret framing
the bank has no `could` row - the writer tags the surface `could` with the A1 concept `can`, which is available from the start
`must` is A1 and `asleep`/`tired`/`at home` are prior; the deduction reading is a use, not new vocabulary
`to need` is A2 (the B1 `need` row is the noun `der Bedarf` and must not be used here); `You needn't bring anything` is writable at once

`used to (habit)` is introduced in lesson 31 (`talking about earlier times`) alongside `former` and `ever since`; the plain B1 `used to` means `accustomed` and is a different concept, taught much later
there is no `ought to` concept - the writer tags the surface `ought to` with A1 `should`, so the topic is open from lesson 1
`who` and `which` are A1; lesson 11 (`character and relationships`) and lesson 58 (`family and friends`) give people to add extra information about
`whose`, `where` and `when` are all A1 concepts in the prior pool

as...as works from lesson 1 with A1 `as`, but the result pattern is safest once `so that (result)` arrives in lesson 27 (`linking causes`); `rather than` cannot be written because the bank has no `than` row
`much` and `a bit` are A1 and `even` is A2, so `much better` and `colder and colder` are writable straight away
the `the problem is that...` pattern wants a noun to head it; lesson 5 (`problems and solutions`) supplies `problem`-style heads (`situation`, `solution`, `condition`), and the possessive 's is glue
`much`, `many`, `most`, `half`, `none` and `a bit` are A1, `enough` is A2; the whole range is prior-level
`to pick up`, `to turn on` and `to turn off` are A1; lesson 41 (`computers and chores`) and lesson 178 in the final order (`switching things on`) widen the set
the three-part verbs of this level are B1 concepts: `to rely on`, `to take advantage of` and `to be worth the effort` all land in lesson 40 (`brands and buying`)
`to want` (A1), `to tell` (A1) and `to ask` (A2) already take this pattern; `to expect` joins them in lesson 19
`to let` and `to help` are A1; the bank has no `to make` row, so the make half of the topic cannot be shown and let/help have to carry it

`although` and `so that` are A2, but lesson 27 (`linking causes`) is where `since (because)`, `because of`, `thanks to`, `so that (result)` and `after (conjunction)` arrive together, which is what makes all three relations writable
the opening -ing clause usually names a state; lesson 9 (`feelings`) plus A2 `tired` give `Feeling tired, she went to bed early` its content
`firstly` is A1, but the contrast and addition halves are B1: `in addition` arrives in lesson 25 and `on the one hand` / `on the other hand` in lesson 30; `secondly` is missing from the bank
tags are built from auxiliaries and pronouns only, all A1; `right` (A2) covers the informal tag
`someone`, `something`, `anything` and `or` are A1, so both the relative-clause focus and the vague `or something` are writable from lesson 1
`one` is A1; lesson 12 (`confidence and effort`) and lesson 11 (`character and relationships`) give `polite`, `honest` and `responsible`, the adjectives generic `one` is normally used with

the bank has no `ourselves`/`yourselves`/`themselves` rows, so only the emphatic half is supportable, through A2 `myself` and A1 `oneself`; lesson 29 adds `each other`, which is reciprocal rather than reflexive
`at home` is A1 and `another` is A2; `the other` has no bank row, so `another` has to carry that half
`will`, `not` and the -ing form are all prior-level; lesson 33 (`plans, dates and deadlines`) later supplies the future times to deny
`to go`, `to be` and `to forget` are A1/A2, so `I was going to call you, but I forgot` needs nothing from B1
the pattern is it + be + focus + that, built from A1 words; lesson 2 (`reasons and results`) gives the reasons a cleft usually focuses
